text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Pleurobrachia
(B) Ascaris
(C) Pila
(D) Balanoglossus
List-II
(I) Excretion through proboscis gland
(II) Well-marked bioluminescence
(III) Pseudocoelomate body
(IV) File-like rasping organ (radula) in the mouth
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV
A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
solution: Pleurobrachia is a ctenophore, a group in which bioluminescence is well marked. Ascaris (Aschelminthes) is pseudocoelomate. Pila (Mollusca) has a radula in its mouth. Balanoglossus (Hemichordata) excretes through the proboscis gland. So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In cartilaginous fishes (Chondrichthyes), the notochord persists throughout life.
Statement II: In bony fishes (Osteichthyes), the heart is three-chambered.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: NCERT says that in Chondrichthyes the notochord persists throughout life, so Statement I is true. Fishes, both cartilaginous and bony, have a two-chambered heart (one auricle and one ventricle), so Statement II is false.

text:
How many of the following animals are cold-blooded (poikilothermous)?
Pteropus, Chelone, Hyla, Exocoetus, Columba, Delphinus, Calotes, Naja
solution: Chelone (turtle), Calotes (garden lizard) and Naja (cobra) are reptiles, Hyla (tree frog) is an amphibian and Exocoetus (flying fish) is a bony fish. All five are cold-blooded. Pteropus (flying fox) and Delphinus (dolphin) are mammals and Columba (pigeon) is a bird, so these three are warm-blooded. Answer: 5.

text:
Choose the correct statements:
A. In sponges, choanocytes (collar cells) line the spongocoel and the canals.
B. Cnidoblasts of coelenterates are used for anchorage, defence and capture of prey.
C. Platyhelminthes are pseudocoelomate animals.
D. Flame cells help in osmoregulation and excretion in Platyhelminthes.
E. Arthropods have a closed type of circulatory system.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, C and D only
B, D and E only
A, B and D only
A, B, C and D only
solution: A, B and D are NCERT statements. C is wrong because flatworms are acoelomate. E is wrong because arthropods have an open circulatory system. So the answer is A, B and D only.

text: Which one of the following statements about the cockroach (Periplaneta americana) is correct?
options: Malpighian tubules are present at the junction of the foregut and the midgut
Each compound eye consists of about 2000 hexagonal ommatidia
The ventral nerve cord has three ganglia in the abdomen and six in the thorax
The mushroom-shaped gland is present in the 2nd and 3rd abdominal segments
solution: Each compound eye of a cockroach has about 2000 hexagonal ommatidia, which gives mosaic vision. Malpighian tubules lie at the junction of the midgut and the hindgut. The nerve cord has three ganglia in the thorax and six in the abdomen. The mushroom-shaped gland lies in the 6th and 7th abdominal segments.

text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Malonate inhibits the activity of the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase.
Reason R: Malonate closely resembles the substrate succinate in structure and competes with it for the active site of the enzyme.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: Malonate is the NCERT example of a competitive inhibitor. It looks like succinate, binds to the active site of succinic dehydrogenase and blocks the substrate. Both statements are true, and R explains A.

text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Oxidoreductases
(B) Transferases
(C) Hydrolases
(D) Lyases
List-II
(I) Remove groups from substrates by mechanisms other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds
(II) Catalyse oxidation-reduction between two substrates S and S'
(III) Catalyse transfer of a group G (other than hydrogen) between a pair of substrates

solution: Oxidoreductases carry out redox reactions (II). Transferases transfer a group other than hydrogen (III). Hydrolases break bonds by hydrolysis (IV). Lyases remove groups without hydrolysis and leave double bonds (I). So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

text:
Choose the correct statements:
A. In a polysaccharide chain such as glycogen, the right end is called the reducing end and the left end the non-reducing end.
B. Cellulose gives a blue colour with iodine because it holds $I_2$ in its helices.
C. Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world.
D. RuBisCO is the most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere.
E. Inulin is a polymer of glucose.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, C and D only
A, B and E only
B, C and D only
C, D and E only
solution: A, C and D are NCERT facts. B is wrong: starch forms helices that hold $I_2$ and turn blue, but cellulose has no complex helices and cannot hold $I_2$. E is wrong because inulin is a polymer of fructose. Answer: A, C and D only.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The partial pressures of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the alveolar air are about 104 mm Hg and 40 mm Hg respectively.
Statement II: Under normal physiological conditions, every 100 mL of deoxygenated blood delivers approximately 4 mL of $CO_2$ to the alveoli.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: According to the NCERT table, alveolar $pO_2$ is 104 mm Hg and $pCO_2$ is 40 mm Hg. NCERT also says that every 100 mL of deoxygenated blood delivers about 4 mL of $CO_2$ to the alveoli. Both statements are true.

text: In a healthy adult, tidal volume = 500 mL, inspiratory reserve volume = 3000 mL, expiratory reserve volume = 1100 mL and residual volume = 1200 mL. The inspiratory capacity and the functional residual capacity respectively are:
options: 4600 mL and 2300 mL
3500 mL and 1600 mL
5800 mL and 2300 mL
3500 mL and 2300 mL
solution: Inspiratory capacity = TV + IRV = 500 + 3000 = 3500 mL. Functional residual capacity = ERV + RV = 1100 + 1200 = 2300 mL.

text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) P-wave
(B) QRS complex
(C) T-wave
(D) End of the T-wave
List-II
(I) Depolarisation of the ventricles
(II) End of systole
(III) Depolarisation (excitation) of the atria
(IV) Return of the ventricles from excited to normal state
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
solution: The P-wave shows atrial depolarisation and the QRS complex shows ventricular depolarisation. The T-wave shows the ventricles returning to the normal state (repolarisation), and the end of the T-wave marks the end of systole. So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The plasma of a person with blood group O contains both anti-A and anti-B antibodies.
Statement II: Erythroblastosis foetalis can occur when an Rh-negative foetus is carried by an Rh-positive mother.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: Blood group O has no A or B antigens on its RBCs, and its plasma has both anti-A and anti-B, so Statement I is true. Erythroblastosis foetalis happens when an Rh-negative mother carries an Rh-positive foetus, the reverse of what Statement II says. So Statement II is false.

text:
Choose the correct statements about the human heart:
A. The SA node can generate the maximum number of action potentials, i.e., 70-75 per minute.
B. The duration of one cardiac cycle is 0.8 second.
C. Atrial systole increases the flow of blood into the ventricles by about 70 per cent.
D. The first heart sound (lub) is associated with the closure of the semilunar valves.
E. The cardiac output of a healthy individual averages about 5 litres per minute.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B and C only
B, D and E only
A, B and E only
A, C and E only
solution: A, B and E are correct (72 beats/min × 70 mL is about 5 L/min). C is wrong because atrial systole adds only about 30 per cent to ventricular filling. D is wrong because 'lub' comes from the closure of the AV (tricuspid and bicuspid) valves; 'dub' comes from the semilunar valves.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The descending limb of the loop of Henle is impermeable to water but permeable to electrolytes.
Statement II: The increasing osmolarity towards the inner medullary interstitium is mainly caused by NaCl and urea.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: The descending limb is permeable to water and almost impermeable to electrolytes; the ascending limb is the reverse. So Statement I is false. The medullary osmotic gradient (300 to about 1200 $\text{mOsmol L}^{-1}$) is mainly due to NaCl and urea, so Statement II is true.

text:
Match List-I with List-II:

A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II
solution: Planaria uses protonephridia (flame cells) and the earthworm uses nephridia. Cockroaches and other insects use Malpighian tubules, and crustaceans like the prawn use antennal (green) glands. So A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I.

text:
Choose the correct statements regarding renal function in humans:
A. GFR in a healthy individual is about 125 mL per minute, i.e., 180 litres per day.
B. Nearly 99 per cent of the glomerular filtrate is reabsorbed by the renal tubules.
C. Atrial natriuretic factor (ANF) causes vasoconstriction and thereby increases blood pressure.
D. Angiotensin II activates the adrenal cortex to release aldosterone.
E. A fall in GFR can activate the JG cells to release renin.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B and C only
A, C, D and E only
B, C and E only
A, B, D and E only
solution: A, B, D and E are NCERT statements. C is wrong: ANF causes vasodilation and lowers blood pressure, which is why it checks the renin-angiotensin mechanism. Answer: A, B, D and E only.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: During contraction of a skeletal muscle fibre, the length of the A-band decreases.
Statement II: During muscle contraction, $Ca^{2+}$ binds to tropomyosin and unmasks the myosin-binding sites on actin.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: During contraction the A-band keeps its length while the I-bands shorten, so Statement I is false. $Ca^{2+}$ binds to a subunit of troponin, not tropomyosin, and this removes the masking of the active sites, so Statement II is also false.

text:
How many of the following statements about the human skeleton are correct?
(i) The skull is composed of 22 bones.
(ii) The vertebral column is formed by 26 serially arranged units.
(iii) The 8th, 9th and 10th pairs of ribs are called floating ribs.
(iv) Each limb is made of 30 bones.
(v) The pectoral girdle is formed by the ilium, ischium and pubis.
(vi) A single U-shaped hyoid bone is present at the base of the buccal cavity.
solution: (i) 8 cranial + 14 facial = 22, correct. (ii) Correct. (iii) Wrong: ribs 8 to 10 are vertebrochondral (false) ribs, and the 11th and 12th pairs are floating ribs. (iv) Correct. (v) Wrong: ilium, ischium and pubis form the pelvic girdle (coxal bone). (vi) Correct. So 4 are correct.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disease of the neuromuscular junction (III). Muscular dystrophy is genetic degeneration of skeletal muscle (IV). Tetany is caused by low $Ca^{2+}$ (I). Gout is caused by uric acid crystals in the joints (II).

text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: In a resting neuron, the outer surface of the axonal membrane is positively charged with respect to the inner surface.
Reason R: The sodium-potassium pump transports 3 $Na^+$ outwards for every 2 $K^+$ into the cell.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: NCERT explains that the Na-K pump moves 3 $Na^+$ out for every 2 $K^+$ in. As a result, the outer surface carries a positive charge and the inner surface a negative charge, so the membrane is polarised. Both statements are true, and R explains A.

List-II

(B) Thyrocalcitonin
(C) Thymosins

List-II
(I) Differentiation of T-lymphocytes

solution: Melatonin from the pineal gland regulates the diurnal rhythm. Thyrocalcitonin (TCT) from the thyroid regulates blood calcium. Thymosins from the thymus help T-lymphocytes differentiate. Erythropoietin from the JG cells of the kidney stimulates RBC formation. So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Hormones which interact with membrane-bound receptors normally do not enter the target cell, but generate second messengers such as cyclic AMP.
Statement II: Steroid hormones and iodothyronines interact with intracellular receptors and mostly regulate gene expression.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: Both statements describe the two mechanisms of hormone action in NCERT. Protein and peptide hormones act through membrane receptors and second messengers such as cAMP, IP3 and $Ca^{2+}$. Steroid hormones and thyroid hormones bind intracellular receptors and act on genes. Both are true.

text:
Choose the correct statements:
A. Low secretion of growth hormone results in stunted growth called pituitary dwarfism.
B. Diabetes insipidus is caused by insufficient secretion of insulin.
C. Graves' disease (exophthalmic goitre) is a form of hypothyroidism.
D. Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes defective development of the growing baby, leading to cretinism.
E. Excess secretion of growth hormone in adults, especially in middle age, causes acromegaly.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B and D only
A, D and E only
C, D and E only
A, B, C and E only
solution: A, D and E are correct. B is wrong because diabetes insipidus comes from a defect in the synthesis or release of ADH (vasopressin), not insulin. C is wrong because Graves' disease is a form of hyperthyroidism. Answer: A, D and E only.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Each primary spermatocyte contains 23 chromosomes.
Statement II: The release of sperms from the seminiferous tubules is called spermiation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: Primary spermatocytes are diploid with 46 chromosomes. Only after meiosis I do the secondary spermatocytes have 23. So Statement I is false. The release of sperms from the seminiferous tubules is called spermiation, so Statement II is true. (Spermiogenesis is the change of spermatids into sperms.)

text:
Choose the correct statements about the human menstrual cycle:
A. The menstrual phase, when menstrual flow occurs, lasts for 3-5 days.
B. Both LH and FSH attain a peak level in the middle of the cycle (about the 14th day).
C. The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone, which is essential for maintenance of the endometrium.
D. Regeneration of the endometrium in the follicular phase is brought about by a high level of progesterone.
E. The rapid secretion of LH (LH surge) induces rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of the ovum.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B and D only
B, C, D and E only
A, C and D only
A, B, C and E only
solution: A, B, C and E follow NCERT. D is wrong: in the follicular phase the endometrium regenerates under the rising level of oestrogens from the growing follicles. Progesterone comes from the corpus luteum in the luteal phase. Answer: A, B, C and E only.

(C) Inner cell mass
(D) Chorionic villi
List-II
(I) Outer layer of the blastocyst that gets attached to the endometrium
(II) Embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres

text: Which of the following statements about human oogenesis is incorrect?
options: Oogenesis is initiated during the embryonic development stage, when a couple of million oogonia are formed within each fetal ovary
No more oogonia are formed and added after birth
The secondary oocyte completes its second meiotic division before it is released from the ovary
The primary oocytes enter prophase-I of meiosis and get temporarily arrested at that stage
solution: The secondary oocyte is released at ovulation while still in meiosis II. It completes the second meiotic division only when a sperm enters it during fertilisation, forming the ovum and a second polar body. The other three statements are correct.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In intra-uterine transfer (IUT), embryos with up to 8 blastomeres are transferred into the fallopian tube.
Statement II: In intra-cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), the sperm is directly injected into the uterus of the female.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: Embryos with up to 8 blastomeres go into the fallopian tube in ZIFT. In IUT, embryos with more than 8 blastomeres go into the uterus. So Statement I is false. In ICSI, the sperm is injected directly into the ovum in the laboratory, not into the uterus, so Statement II is also false.

text:
How many of the following sexually transmitted infections are completely curable if detected early and treated properly?
Gonorrhoea, Syphilis, Genital herpes, Chlamydiasis, Hepatitis-B, Trichomoniasis, Genital warts, HIV infection
solution: NCERT: except for hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infections, other STIs are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. That leaves gonorrhoea, syphilis, chlamydiasis, trichomoniasis and genital warts, which is 5.

text: In a large, randomly mating population that is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium for a gene with two alleles, 16% of the individuals show the recessive phenotype. The frequency of heterozygous individuals in this population is:
solution: $q^2 = 0.16$, so $q = 0.4$ and $p = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$. Heterozygote frequency $= 2pq = 2 \times 0.6 \times 0.4 = 0.48$.

text: Which one of the following is an example of analogous structures, reflecting convergent evolution?
options: Forelimbs of whales, bats and cheetahs
Wings of a butterfly and of a bird
Thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita
Hearts of different vertebrates
solution: The wings of a butterfly and a bird do the same job but have different structure and origin, so they are analogous structures produced by convergent evolution. Vertebrate forelimbs, Bougainvillea thorns with Cucurbita tendrils, and vertebrate hearts are all homologous structures, which point to divergent evolution.

(B) Homo erectus
(C) Neanderthal man
(D) Dryopithecus
List-II
(I) Brain capacity 650-800 cc; probably did not eat meat

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV

solution: Homo habilis had a 650-800 cc brain and probably did not eat meat. Homo erectus (about 1.5 mya) had a brain of about 900 cc and probably ate meat. Neanderthals had a 1400 cc brain, used hides and buried their dead. Dryopithecus (about 15 mya) was hairy and walked like gorillas and chimpanzees. So A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Plasmodium enters the human body as gametocytes through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.
Statement II: The rupture of RBCs infected by Plasmodium releases a toxic substance, haemozoin, which is responsible for the chill and high fever recurring every three to four days.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: Plasmodium enters the human body as sporozoites. Gametocytes form later in the RBCs and are taken up by the mosquito. So Statement I is false. Statement II is true as written in NCERT.

text:
Choose the correct statements about immunity:
A. Each antibody molecule has four peptide chains and is represented as $H_2L_2$.
B. Colostrum secreted by the mother during the initial days of lactation has abundant IgA antibodies.
C. Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) constitutes about 50 per cent of the lymphoid tissue in the human body.
D. Virus-infected cells secrete interferons, which protect non-infected cells from further viral infection.
E. Active immunity is quick and gives a full response immediately.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C and D only
A, B and E only
B, C, D and E only
A, C and E only
solution: A, B, C and D are NCERT statements. E is wrong: active immunity is slow and takes time to give its full effective response. Passive immunity, from ready-made antibodies, is the quick one. Answer: A, B, C and D only.

text: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
options: Cocaine – obtained from the latex of Papaver somniferum
Heroin – chemically diacetylmorphine; acts as a depressant
Cannabinoids – obtained from the coca plant Erythroxylum coca
Smack – a cannabinoid obtained from the inflorescences of Cannabis sativa
solution: Heroin (smack) is diacetylmorphine, made by acetylating morphine from the poppy (Papaver somniferum). It is a depressant that slows down body functions. Cocaine comes from Erythroxylum coca, and cannabinoids come from Cannabis sativa. Smack is heroin, not a cannabinoid.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: EcoRI cuts the DNA between bases G and A only when the sequence GAATTC is present in the DNA.
Statement II: In the naming of restriction enzymes, the Roman numerals following the name indicate the number of recognition sites the enzyme has in a DNA molecule.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: Statement I is the NCERT description of EcoRI. Statement II is false: the Roman numerals show the order in which the enzymes were isolated from that bacterial strain.

text: A foreign DNA fragment is ligated into the PstI site of the vector pBR322, and the recombinant plasmid is introduced into E. coli cells. The transformed cells carrying the recombinant plasmid will:
options: grow on ampicillin but not on tetracycline
grow on both ampicillin and tetracycline
grow on tetracycline but not on ampicillin
grow on neither antibiotic
solution: In pBR322 the PstI site (like PvuI) lies inside the ampicillin resistance gene ($amp^R$). An insert at this site inactivates $amp^R$ by insertional inactivation, while $tet^R$ stays intact. Recombinant cells therefore grow on tetracycline but not on ampicillin.

text:
Choose the correct statements about agarose gel electrophoresis of DNA:
A. DNA fragments, being positively charged, move towards the cathode.
B. Smaller DNA fragments move farther through the gel than larger ones.
C. Agarose is a natural polymer extracted from sea weeds.
D. Separated DNA fragments can be seen in visible light without any staining.
E. DNA stained with ethidium bromide appears as bright orange coloured bands under UV radiation.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B and C only
B, D and E only
A, C and E only
B, C and E only
solution: DNA is negatively charged and moves towards the anode, so A is wrong. Pure DNA cannot be seen in visible light; it is visible only after ethidium bromide staining and UV exposure, so D is wrong. B, C and E are correct.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The Bt toxin protein exists as an inactive protoxin, which is converted into the active form by the alkaline pH of the insect gut.
Statement II: The proteins encoded by the genes cryIAc and cryIIAb control cotton bollworms, while that of cryIAb controls corn borer.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: Both statements are taken from NCERT. The protoxin is solubilised and activated by the alkaline pH of the insect gut, binds to the midgut epithelium, makes pores and kills the insect. cryIAc and cryIIAb target cotton bollworms and cryIAb targets corn borer.

text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) ADA deficiency treatment
(B) Rosie
(C) ELISA
(D) RNA interference
List-II
(I) Silencing of a specific mRNA by a complementary dsRNA
(II) Early detection of pathogens based on antigen-antibody interaction
(III) Gene therapy using lymphocytes
(IV) Milk containing human alpha-lactalbumin
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
solution: ADA deficiency was the first disease treated by gene therapy, using lymphocytes given a functional ADA cDNA. Rosie, the transgenic cow, gave milk with human alpha-lactalbumin. ELISA works on antigen-antibody interaction. RNAi silences a specific mRNA with a complementary dsRNA. So A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Mature human insulin does not contain the C-peptide that is present in proinsulin.
Reason R: In 1983, Eli Lilly prepared two DNA sequences corresponding to the A and B chains of human insulin and introduced them into plasmids of E. coli.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: Insulin is made as a pro-hormone. The extra C-peptide is removed during maturation, so A is true. R is also true, since Eli Lilly made the A and B chains separately and joined them by disulphide bonds. But R describes how insulin is produced commercially and does not explain why mature insulin lacks the C-peptide.
